page: Google Cloud Platform c4n-highcpu-4 is an entry-level compute-focused instance from the network-optimized family. It is equipped with an Intel Xeon 8581C processor built on the x86_64 architecture, configured with 4 dedicated virtual CPUs across 2 physical cores and hyper-threading enabled at a base frequency of 2.3 GHz. The instance is allocated 8.0 GB of system memory, matching a 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio of 2.0 GB per vCPU. The processor supports advanced hardware instruction sets, including AVX-512 extensions (such as VNNI and BF16) and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX). There is no onboard local storage or discrete GPU acceleration included with this instance profile.

Benchmark data reflects strong per-core performance paired with limited aggregate throughput. The server scores in the top 10% on Geekbench single-core testing (2228.0) and exhibits strong single-threaded data compression and decompression performance. Conversely, multi-threaded throughput metrics such as stress-ng multi-core and bzip3 decompression register in the bottom 25% due to the 4-vCPU ceiling. Memory bandwidth benchmarks also place in the lower tier, recording 32.55 GB/s uncached reads and 20.39 GB/s uncached writes on large memory blocks, which similarly depresses the PassMark memory score.

From an operational and resource perspective, the instance provides high single-thread execution efficiency but faces clear multi-core and memory capacity tradeoffs. With 8 GB of RAM and no bundled local storage, workloads must account for remote block storage configurations and memory footprints. The c4n-highcpu-4 is best matched for single-thread-intensive services, static web serving, network edge services, lightweight database operations, and small model LLM prompt processing.
